name: Hue food guide
summary: Hue eats like the old capital it is: bún bò Huế at Dong Ba, cơm hến on Hen Island, bánh khoái along Kim Long toward Thien Mu, the small steamed cakes, and chè after the meal.
body: Hue eats a beef-and-pork noodle bowl, a clam rice from the river island, a turmeric crepe on the north bank, and small steamed cakes, among them bánh nậm, which Vietnam Tourism ties to the court kitchen. It is not mì Quảng and not cao lầu. Those belong down the coast.

Give the first bowl to Dong Ba market. Cross Ưng Bình bridge to Hen Island for cơm hến or bún hến, and skip the island in a flood week. Kim Long, on the way to Thien Mu, is the road for bánh khoái and bún thịt nướng. Nem lụi is grilled pork on a skewer, wrapped in rice paper with herbs and a creamy sauce. Finish with chè, the sweet soup.
specialtiesLead: The first bowls and cakes are bún bò Huế, cơm hến, bánh bèo, bánh khoái, bánh nậm, and nem lụi.

sections.heading: Also ordered in Hue
paragraphs: Bún thịt nướng is the Kim Long lunch. Bún hến is the other bowl on Hen Island, beside cơm hến. After the meal, the sweet soups are corn, lotus seed, and taro, and a dumpling soup with roast pork.

spots.name: Bun thit nuong
spots.note: Cold rice noodles with hot grilled pork, herbs, green papaya, carrot, cucumber, and lettuce. Hue’s peanut sauce and a sweet-sour fish sauce go on the noodles, then you toss.

spots.name: Bun hen
spots.address: Cồn Hến, across Ưng Bình bridge
spots.note: Rice noodles with the same tiny river clams as cơm hến, sold from the stalls on Hen Island. The island is a walk of under half an hour, and it goes under when the city floods.

spots.name: Corn chè
spots.note: Sweet corn cooked into a thick, glutinous soup. Take it after the meal, a bowl at a time.

spots.name: Lotus-seed chè
spots.note: Lotus seeds in a sweet, glutinous soup. Take it after the meal, a bowl at a time.

spots.name: Taro chè
spots.note: Taro in a sweet soup, taken after the meal.

spots.name: Roast-pork dumpling chè
spots.note: Dumplings of bột lọc, the clear tapioca dough, around roast pork, in a sweet soup. Take it after the meal.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: The doors are markets and roads, not a booked room. Dong Ba is the morning market. Hen Island is the clam rice. Kim Long is the snack road toward Thien Mu. Chi Lăng and Bạch Đằng are the afternoon streets on the far side of the island, and the city’s 2026 tourism plan is building them into a night stop with Hoàng Thành and Bao Vinh.

spots.name: Dong Ba Market
spots.caption: The front of Chợ Đông Ba
spots.note: The city market. Buy produce first, then eat the snacks, bánh khoái and bánh bèo, and a bowl of bún bò Huế inside.

spots.name: Hen Island
spots.note: Cross Ưng Bình bridge and eat cơm hến or bún hến from the stalls. The walk is under half an hour, and the island disappears when the city floods.

spots.name: Kim Long
spots.address: Kim Long, north bank toward Thien Mu
spots.note: The north-bank road toward Thien Mu, for bánh khoái and bún thịt nướng. Go in the daytime, on the pagoda ride.

spots.name: Chi Lang and Bach Dang
spots.note: The afternoon streets past Hen Island. The city’s 2026 plan names them as a night stop in the making, with Hoàng Thành and Bao Vinh.

seoTitle: Hue food guide — bun bo, com hen, cakes, and Kim Long
seoDescription: Bun bo Hue at Dong Ba, com hen on Hen Island, and banh khoai along Kim Long. Nem lui is grilled pork on a skewer, wrapped with herbs and a creamy sauce.
